HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  ORDER % 16.11.2023 CRL.M.A. 31223/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 CrPC seeking quashing of FIR No.16/2013 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Chhawla and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
The learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.
5. He further submits that in the aforesaid FIR seven persons have been arraigned as accused.
However, the present petition has been filed only by

He submits that one of the accused namely Satya, who is the mother-in-law of the respondent no.2 has already expired and no compromise has been arrived at between the respondent no.2 and her husband, as well as, one other sister-in-law, namely, Poonam.
6.
The petitioners, as well as, respondent no. 2 are present in the court and they have been identified by their counsel and by the Investigating Officer SI Menka, PS. Chhawla.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that the respondent no.2 got married to the brother of the petitioners herein on 11.05.2004, according to Hindu Rites and Customs.

Out of the said wedlock,
one female child namely, Sahiba David was born.
8. On account of temperamental issues certain disputes arose between the parties and from 2013 onwards, the respondent no.2 and her husband started residing separately.
The dispute between the parties also led to the registration of present FIR.

9. During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of Memorandum of Understanding dated 27.10.2023, which is annexed as Annexure B to the present petition.

10. It is recorded in the aforesaid settlement that the petitioners, as well as, respondent no.2 have arrived at an amicable settlement and the respondent no.2 has no grievance left against the petitioners.
11. The petitioners on their part have also agreed that they shall accept, recognise and treat the respondent no.2 and her daughter (Sahiba David), as This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/11/2023 at 22:35:51 the wife and daughter, respectively, of their brother Rajan Massi.
12. It is also a term of the settlement that the respondent no.2 shall cooperate with the petitioners for the quashing of the aforesaid FIR.

13. On a query put by the Court, the respondent no.2 states that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed qua the petitioners.
14.
In view of the fact that the parties have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
15. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
16. Consequently, the petition is allowed and the FIR No.16/2013 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Chhawla alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, is quashed.

17. The petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
18. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J NOVEMBER 16, 2023/dss
